info.bio:
Dinosaur Jr es una banda de rock de Amherst, Massachusetts formada en  1983  por J Mascis (guitarra y vocales) y su compañero de secundaria Lou Barlow (bajo), luego de la separación de la banda de hardcore-punk que integraban anteriormente, Deep Wound. Posteriormente se les uniría Emmett Patrick Murphy (batería).

scenes.name: Indie, C86 y el giro retro
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: En 1985 la energía se ha disipado: el new pop cae en la decadencia (Live Aid, «una tragedia para el pop»), los singles independientes venden la mitad que en 1980 y «independiente» se convierte en «indie», un género de guitarras sucias, voces pálidas y nostalgia de los sesenta, oposición impotente al mainstream. El futurismo da paso al «rock de coleccionista»: The Jesus and Mary Chain (Psychocandy: Ronettes y Beach Boys con feedback), el sello Creation y Primal Scream, la cassette C86 de NME (The Pastels, Shop Assistants, The Soup Dragons, June Brides) y su culto a la inocencia, que reaparecerá en el riot grrrl. The Smiths y R.E.M., contra los ochenta; Hüsker Dü, Sonic Youth, Butthole Surfers y Dinosaur Jr. redescubren el acid rock; de ahí, Nirvana.

scenes.name: Noise-rock y noise-pop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Sonic Youth acuñan el «noise-rock»: aún obedece las reglas del rock'n'roll, pero secuestrado por sonidos disonantes. En Nueva York, Rat At Rat R, Agitpop, Ritual Tension, Gut Bank, la triple guitarra de Band Of Susans, Of Cabbages And Kings, Spongehead, Alice Donut. Boston da los grupos más influyentes de la década siguiente: Dinosaur Jr (el estándar «noise-pop», fusión de distorsión y melodía, eslabón entre Sonic Youth y el grunge) y los Pixies (Surfer Rosa, Doolittle). El art-punk del Sur (Antietam, Squirrel Bait, Blind Idiot God, Alter Natives) y los excéntricos de San Francisco (Tragic Mulatto, Slovenly).

podcast.title: Judgment Night Collaboration with Del the Funky Homosapien (1993)
podcast.body: Dinosaur Jr. collaborated with hip-hop artist Del the Funky Homosapien for the 1993 *Judgment Night* soundtrack. This pairing was considered radical at the time due to the limited crossover between rock and hip-hop. The project was a major catalyst for the creation of rap rock and nu metal, and helped bridge the divide between rock and hip-hop fans. "The pairings included Pearl Jam and Cypress Hill, Slayer working with Ice Tea, Faith No More and Buella Tribe, Dinosaur Jr., and Del the Funky Homo sapien, 11 collaborations at all."

podcast.title: 80s American Indie Rock
podcast.body: Dinosaur Jr. is listed as one of the bands grouped under the "American 80s indie rock" umbrella, representing the diverse rock movements in the United States during that decade. "junta a dainers or junior."

srcs.episode: Cuál fue el primer disco de Grunge?

podcast.title: Boston Area Indie Band
podcast.body: Dinosaur Jr. is listed as one of the amazing indie bands that emerged from the Boston area's rich college music scene. "We had Mission of Burma, the Delphwegos, the Lemonheads, Gang Green, the throwing muses, Dinosaur, Junior, Julianne Hatfield and the Blake Babies, and of course the greatest Boston area college band of them all, the Pixies."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 3

podcast.title: Delayed Recognition
podcast.body: Dinosaur Jr. experienced a delayed recognition, similar to My Bloody Valentine and Manic Street Preachers, struggling to gain widespread attention until later due to the lack of early record label support for the Shoegaze-related movement they were part of. "algo muy parecido les acabaría pasando a otras bandas como los Manic Street Richard, o como Dinosaur Junior."

srcs.episode: La generación perdida del Indie: SHOEGAZE

podcast.title: Guitar-Driven Sound
podcast.body: The band is identified with a more guitar-driven sound, which aligns them with the shoegaze tendency, particularly influenced by bands like The Jesus and Mary Chain. "tenemos bandas a lo mejor como de dinosaur junior o los maneguester preachers en sus inicios, que hacían como un sesonido más guitarrero, más en la vertende de Jesus and Mary Chain."

srcs.episode: DREAM POP y SHOEGAZE. Diferencias entre ellos.

podcast.title: Influence on Guitar-Based Genres
podcast.body: Dinosaur Jr.'s dense, melodic, and effects-heavy guitars contributed to defining the emerging guitar-based genres, particularly those derived from the No Wave movement in the United States, which developed a sound that was similar to, but often more aggressive than, its British counterparts. "El doc cargado de kickback de Sonic Youth y las guitarras densas y melodicas, llenas de efectos de Windows Out Junior, también ayudaron a definir el género."

srcs.episode: El disco imposible: La historia de Loveless y My Bloody Valentine

podcast.title: J Mascis in Ron Ashton's Band
podcast.body: J Mascis of Dinosaur Jr. was a member of a band that Ron Ashton played in after The Stooges' initial breakup. "Ron Ashton played in a series of bands, none of which did much, although there was the group that featured Thurston Moore of Sonic Youth, also Mark Arm of Mudhoney and Jay Mascus of Dinosaur Jr."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About The Stooges?

podcast.title: Lofi Classification
podcast.body: Dinosaur Jr. was explicitly considered to be a Lofi band, indicating their contribution to a sound characterized by grittier, less high-tech recordings, often perceived as authentic and real. "We had Dinosaur Jr., Cebado, even Beck, especially as indie label work, were all considered to be Lofi."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Powerpop in Some Songs
podcast.body: Dinosaur Jr. is mentioned as a band that "might fit the bill with some songs" when it comes to Powerpop. This indicates that while not entirely a Powerpop band, certain tracks exhibit characteristics of the genre, showcasing its diverse reach within alternative rock. "Dinosaur Jr. might fit the bill with some songs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Shoegaze DNA Contributor
podcast.body: Dinosaur Jr., particularly through J. Mascis's work, is cited as a significant contributor to the "DNA" of shoegaze music. Their characteristic "fuzzy guitars and vulnerable introspective lyrics" blended well with other emerging sounds that would define the genre. "J. Mascus and Dinosaur Jr., for example, have a lot to answer for, with their fuzzy guitars and vulnerable introspective lyrics."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
